claim_summary: Presents a purported AI-assisted combination therapy as having cured advanced liver cancer without a traceable primary source.
Suggests an improvised half-dose analgesic trial in a breastfeeding patient instead of a drug-specific, clinician-supervised assessment.
Implies that an AI follow-up alert can lead directly to a remote instruction to add medication without documenting clinical reassessment boundaries.
Uses simplified treatment selection and suggests early ambulation can avoid anticoagulation after joint replacement.
Provides disease-level antibiotic and procedure choices as generic cost-control examples without patient-specific indications or contraindications.
